arxiv-2103-15082.title: Conductance zeros in complex molecules and lattices from the interference set method
arxiv-2103-15082.creator: M. Niţă, M. Ţolea, D. C. Marinescu
arxiv-2103-15082.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by M. Niţă, M. Ţolea, D. C. Marinescu. Destructive quantum interference (DQI) and its effects on electron transport is studied in chemical molecules and finite physical lattices that can be described by a discrete Hamiltonian. Starting from a bipartite system whose conductance zeros are known to exist between any two points of a specially designated set, the interference set, we use the Dyson equation to develop a general algorithm of determining the zero conductance points in complex systems, which are not necessarily bipartite.

arxiv-2301-12836.title: Integral equation method for microseismic wavefield modelling in anisotropic elastic media
arxiv-2301-12836.creator: Ujjwal Shekhar
arxiv-2301-12836.description: Abstract ABSTRACT In this paper, we present a frequency-domain volume integral method to model the microseismic wavefield in heterogeneous anisotropic-elastic media. The elastic wave equation is written as an integral equation of the Lippmann-Schwinger type, and the seismic source is represented as a general moment tensor.

arxiv-2405-01686.title: Automatically Extracting Numerical Results from Randomized Controlled Trials with Large Language Models
arxiv-2405-01686.creator: Hye Sun Yun, David Pogrebitskiy, Iain J. Marshall, Byron C. Wallace
arxiv-2405-01686.description: Abstract Meta-analyses statistically aggregate the findings of different randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to assess treatment effectiveness. Because this yields robust estimates of treatment effectiveness, results from meta-analyses are considered the strongest form of evidence. However, rigorous evidence syntheses are time-consuming and labor-intensive, requiring manual extraction of data from individual trials to be synthesized.

arxiv-2507-11217.title: Quantum Adaptive Excitation Network with Variational Quantum Circuits for Channel Attention
arxiv-2507-11217.creator: Yu-Chao Hsu 1 2 , Kuan-Cheng Chen 3 4 , Tai-Yue Li 2 and Nan-Yow Chen 2
arxiv-2507-11217.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yu-Chao Hsu 1 2 , Kuan-Cheng Chen 3 4 , Tai-Yue Li 2 and Nan-Yow Chen 2. In this work, we introduce the Quantum Adaptive Excitation Network (QAE-Net), a hybrid quantum-classical framework designed to enhance channel attention mechanisms in Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). QAE-Net replaces the classical excitation block of Squeeze-and-Excitation modules with a shallow Variational Quantum Circuit (VQC), leveraging quantum superposition and entanglement to capture higher-order inter-channel dependencies that are challenging to model with purely classical approaches.

arxiv-2512-13442.title: XNNTab – Interpretable Neural Networks for Tabular Data using Sparse Autoencoders
arxiv-2512-13442.creator: Khawla Elhadri, Jörg Schlötterer, Christin Seifert
arxiv-2512-13442.description: Abstract In data-driven applications relying on tabular data, where interpretability is key, machine learning models such as decision trees and linear regression are applied. Although neural networks can provide higher predictive performance, they are not used because of their blackbox nature. In this work, we present XNNTab , a neural architecture that combines the expressiveness of neural networks and interpretability.

arxiv-2512-16768.title: On The Hidden Biases of Flow Matching Samplers
arxiv-2512-16768.creator: Soon Hoe Lim 1,2 1 Department of Mathematics, KTH Royal Institute of Technology 2 Nordita, KTH Royal Institute of Technology and Stockholm University
arxiv-2512-16768.description: Abstract We study the implicit bias of flow matching (FM) samplers via the lens of empirical flow matching. Although population FM may produce gradient-field velocities resembling optimal transport (OT), we show that the empirical FM minimizer is generally not a gradient field, even when each conditional flow is. Consequently, empirical FM is intrinsically not OT-optimal in the Benamou-Brenier sense.

pmc-12995773.creator: Rutong Wang, Yingqi Feng, Ziyu Zhou, Jiajun Jiang, Runze Zhang, Wenhui Zou, Haotian Yang, Wenbo Lv, Shen Yang
pmc-12995773.description: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) research has transcended the traditional paradigm centered on amyloid-beta (Aβ) shifting toward a neuroimmune network perspective. pmc-13336056.title: A Piezo‐Mimetic Ionic Hydrogel Harnessing Joint Motion for Cartilage Repair
pmc-13336056.creator: Chenyuan Gao, Xinyu Wang, Zhifeng Wu, Xinya Zhang, Xiao Geng, Ti Zhang, Yue Wang, Hongwei Xia, Jun Zhang, Xianbo Qiu, Cuiru Sun, Yingjie Yu, Wenli Dai, Hua Tian, Qing Cai
pmc-13336056.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Articular cartilage regeneration remains challenging due to its avascular architecture and limited intrinsic repair capacity. Here, we present a piezo‐mimetic ionic hydrogel (PSG‐Mgc) that harnesses endogenous joint motion to orchestrate cartilage repair through mechano‐electrical coupling. The hydrogel integrates a freeze‐thaw crosslinked poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) backbone for mechanical resilience with sodium alginate (SA) and carboxyl‐enriched acylated gelatin (Acy‐Gel) to construct a hydrated, ion‐permissive network capable of dynamic Mg2+ coordination.
